subject: DPA: data lifecycle carve-outs, subprocessors & e-sign logistics
messages:

Cc: OptimaHealth Legal <legal@optimahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Optima DPA redlines - backups/DR and subprocessors

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — product looked great and the latency numbers were impressive. Legal at OptimaHealth asked me to send over our initial DPA redlines (attached) and call out two items specifically where we need confirmation before we can move to e-sign:

1) Backup/DR carve-out: we have a standard clause where backup copies are exempt from immediate deletion requests for up to 90 days and may be retained for DR purposes. Can Redwood accept a 90-day backup retention carve-out, and will you commit to not using backups for any other processing?

2) Subprocessors & international transfers: we need a current subprocessors list and an explicit mechanism for notice & objection. Also — Optima requires EU transfer safeguards (SCCs or equivalent) for any EU personal data.

We attached our redlines to the DPA (Optima_DPA_v3_redlines.pdf). Assuming we can align on the backup language and the subprocessors/transfer approach, legal has asked that we execute via DocuSign so procurement can close the PO quickly.

Could you confirm next steps and timeline? Ideally we close legal review this week so our procurement folks can issue the PO.

Thanks,
Sam

OptimaHealth

Hi Sam — great to hear, and thanks for sending the redlines. We’re excited to get OptimaHealth onboard. Quick responses to your two asks and proposed next steps below.

Backup/DR carve-out
- We can accept a limited backup/DR carve-out, with the following constraints: backups retained for DR only (no operational processing), retention capped at 90 days from snapshot, and we will apply secure access controls and encryption in place for backups.
- We’ll add a certified-deletion clause: if you request deletions, we will remove live copies immediately and exclude restore of deleted data; for restored backups we will certify deletion of the restored data on request (see Neha’s forthcoming suggested language).

Subprocessors & transfers
- We’ll provide the current subprocessors list (and a notice window of 30 days for material additions).
- For EU transfers, we can adopt SCCs (we use the current EDPB standard clauses) or rely on an approved mechanism you prefer; we’ll include standard language in the DPA.

E-sign and timeline
- If that approach works, we’ll circulate Redwood-approved DPA language today and prepare a DocuSign envelope for signature. Rishi — can you confirm we can set the envelope to require signatures from both OptimaHealth’s legal signer and our authorized signatory?
- Neha — looping you for approved wording on the backup carve-out and the certified-deletion flow. If you can provide language this morning, I’ll send to Sam and OptimaLegal and kick off DocuSign.

Next steps:
- Neha to provide legal-approved redline for backup/DR deletion carve-out (target: today).
- Marissa to update DPA with agreed language and send DocuSign envelope (target: today).
- Optima to confirm acceptance of SCCs or propose alternative transfer mechanism.

Sam — thanks again. If you want to hop on a quick 20-min call to align language, happy to do so.

Best,

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>

Subject: Fwd: Optima DPA redlines - backups/DR and subprocessors — internal notes

Neha / Rishi — forwarding Optima’s redlines and my reply below. Key asks from their side: 90-day backup carve-out (standard), explicit SCCs for EU transfers, 30-day notice for subprocessors. Optima wants to execute via DocuSign once we align.

My suggested pragmatic positions (open to legal tweaks):
- Accept 90-day backup carve-out but add: (a) backups used only for DR (no analytics/processing), (b) ability to certify deletion of restored data within 30 days upon request, and (c) documented retention schedule in Exhibit B.
- Subprocessors: 30-day notice + ability for Optima to object in writing; if objection material and unresolved, right to suspend processing for that data category (this is their redline — seems heavy). Recommend we offer an objection+remediation process but not suspension unless regulatory requirement.
- Transfers: we already have SCCs in place — propose we reference SCCs in Section X and attach executed SCCs as part of the DPA.

Questions for legal:
1) Is the certified-deletion wording below defensible (I drafted a short clause in the doc): 
   • On deletion request, Redwood will promptly delete live production data and will not use or restore deleted data from backups. If restoration of backups is required for recovery, Redwood will, within 30 days of restoration, identify and permanently delete any data elements covered by the deletion request and certify in writing to Optima.
2) Can we agree to a 30-day notification for subprocessors but limit customer objection remedies to commercially reasonable measures and escalation to legal (i.e., avoid suspension)?

I’ve attached Optima’s redlines to this thread. If Neha can provide language we can send back to Optima and prepare DocuSign today, that would keep procurement timing intact.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference>

Subject: Re: Optima DPA redlines - backups/DR and subprocessors — proposed language

Marissa / Rishi / Sam / Optima Legal — thanks for the clear summary. Below is Redwood’s suggested DPA language (clean and redline available on request). This is intended to be definitive for the current deal so we can move to DocuSign.

1) Backup & DR carve-out (proposed clause):
"Backups and Disaster Recovery. Customer acknowledges that Provider may create backups and replicas of Customer Data for disaster recovery and operational resiliency. Such backup copies shall be used solely for disaster recovery purposes and not for any other processing activities. Provider may retain backup copies for a period not to exceed ninety (90) days from snapshot. In the event Customer issues a deletion request, Provider will (i) promptly delete Customer Data from live production systems, (ii) exclude the deleted Customer Data from any future restores, and (iii) if restoration of backups is necessary to effectuate disaster recovery, Provider will identify and permanently delete any restored instances of the deleted Customer Data within thirty (30) days of restoration and provide Customer with written certification of such deletion"

2) Subprocessors (proposed clause):
"Subprocessors. Provider will maintain an up-to-date list of subprocessors and provide Customer with at least thirty (30) days' prior notice of the addition of any new subprocessor. Customer may reasonably object in writing to the appointment of a new subprocessor within such notice period on legitimate data protection grounds. In the event of a timely objection, the parties will use commercially reasonable efforts to resolve the objection in good faith. If the parties are unable to resolve such objection, Provider may, at its option, (a) offer to use an alternative subprocessor agreeable to Customer, or (b) suspend processing of the impacted Customer Data only to the extent required by applicable law. Provider will not be required to suspend processing where doing so would be unlawful or would materially impair Provider’s ability to provide the Services."

3) International transfers
- We will incorporate the current EDPB SCCs into the DPA as Exhibit C. If Optima requires a different mechanism, please flag and we’ll review.

DocuSign flow / exhibits
- Marissa: please prepare the DocuSign envelope and include Exhibit B (Retention Schedule), Exhibit C (SCCs) and an Attachment listing current subprocessors. I recommend setting signing order to: Optima legal signer -> Redwood authorized signatory.
- Optima Legal: once you confirm the SCC approach and the backup clause above, we’ll upload the final DPA to DocuSign and aim for signatures today.

Attachments: Redwood_approved_DPA_retention_clauses_v1.docx (contains the clause text above and sample Exhibit B).

If anyone wants to talk through line-by-line, I’m available in the afternoon.
